skill.name: email-notify
skill.description: Send SMTP email notifications when a Codex or Claude task finishes, with device, project, status, and summary details.
skill.summary: Send task completion notifications through a user-configured SMTP email account.
skill.author: caopulan

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally sends SMTP email through user-configured settings and reads SMTP credentials from environment variables. I confirmed the outbound email capability and shell-profile credential guidance, and dismissed markdown backtick and system reconnaissance matches as false positives.

remediation.issue: SMTP credentials are documented for shell startup files.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a dedicated secret manager or a restricted-permission env file instead of exporting CODEX_EMAIL_PASSWORD globally.

remediation.issue: Task summaries can be sent outside the local workspace by email.
remediation.suggestion: Keep notifications minimal, sanitize summaries, and document that secrets and private data must not be included.

remediation.issue: Outbound SMTP delivery depends on user-provided recipients and server settings.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user opt-in before first use and encourage dry-run verification of recipients and transport mode.

content.value_statement: Codex runs can finish when you are away from the terminal. This skill sends SMTP email notifications with status, project, device, and summary details.
actual_capabilities: Sends plain text task completion emails through SMTP or SMTPS.
Supports STARTTLS or SSL, with validation that only one mode is enabled.
Includes device, project, status, and summary fields in each notification.
Reads the project name from AGENTS.md or the current folder.
Supports multiple recipients separated by commas or semicolons.
Provides a dry-run mode for checking settings without sending email.
limitations: Requires user-managed SMTP server settings and recipient addresses.
Does not provide OAuth setup, provider-specific APIs, or credential rotation.
Sends plain text notifications only, without attachments or rich templates.
The user must prevent secrets from being included in task summaries.

use_cases.title: Remote Task Monitoring
use_cases.description: Receive an email when a long Codex run finishes, including project name, status, and a short summary.

use_cases.title: Team Build Awareness
use_cases.description: Notify a small team when an agent completes a repository task that needs review or follow-up.

use_cases.title: Workstation Status Alerts
use_cases.description: Identify which machine completed a task when multiple development devices run AI coding agents.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Basic Completion Email
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup after a single successful task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use email-notify to send a success notification for this completed task. Include the project name and a one-sentence summary.

prompt_templates.title: Notify About a Partial Result
prompt_templates.scenario: Report useful progress when some work remains.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use email-notify to send a partial status email. Summarize what changed, what remains, and avoid including secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Settings Before Sending
prompt_templates.scenario: Check recipient and SMTP configuration safely.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use email-notify in dry-run mode for this project. Show the notification details without sending the email.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Team Handoff Notice
prompt_templates.prompt: Use email-notify to send a concise handoff email after this agent run. Include status, review needs, and any blocker summary.

output_examples.input: Send a success notification for a finished dependency update.
output_examples.output: An email is prepared with the task title, success status, device name, project name, and a short dependency update summary.

output_examples.input: Notify the team that a task is blocked by missing credentials.
output_examples.output: A blocked status email is sent with a concise summary of the missing credential requirement and no secret values.

output_examples.input: Run a dry check before enabling notifications.
output_examples.output: The tool prints the SMTP host, port, sender, recipients, subject, and body without sending a message.

best_practices: Use dry-run mode when configuring a new SMTP account or recipient list.
Keep summaries short and remove secrets, tokens, customer data, and private URLs.
Store SMTP credentials with the least exposure possible and rotate them regularly.
anti_patterns: Do not send full logs, stack traces, tokens, or private customer data in summaries.
Do not configure broad recipient lists for sensitive project notifications.
Do not enable both STARTTLS and SSL for the same SMTP connection.

faq.question: What email service does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the SMTP server configured by the user through environment variables.

faq.question: Can it send to more than one recipient?
faq.answer: Yes. The recipient setting accepts multiple addresses separated by commas or semicolons.

faq.question: Does it support secure SMTP transport?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports STARTTLS or SSL, but only one transport mode should be enabled.

faq.question: Will it detect the project name automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It can read a project name from AGENTS.md or use the current folder name.

faq.question: Does it store email credentials for me?
faq.answer: No. Users provide credentials through their own environment configuration.

faq.question: Should task summaries include sensitive data?
faq.answer: No. Summaries should be brief and should exclude secrets, tokens, customer data, and private links.
